note: Provisional Week 1 baseline prompt set. The canonical prompt set and the fixed token counts are a Week 2 decision (see benchmarks/methodology.md, 'Not yet decided') — this set exists only so the concurrency-1 row can be produced now. Prompts are deliberately close in tokenized length so the aggregates stay comparable; baseline_runner.py records prompt_tokens per request and flags a wide spread.
prompts: Explain what a hash join is and when a query planner picks it over a nested loop join.
Describe how a write-ahead log lets a relational database recover after a crash.
Explain the difference between optimistic and pessimistic concurrency control.
Describe what a covering index is and why it can speed up a read query.
Explain how a bloom filter trades accuracy for memory when answering a lookup.
Describe the role of a memtable and an SST file in a log-structured merge tree.
Explain why connection pooling matters for a service that talks to a database.
Describe what happens during the prefill phase of transformer inference.
